details: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at the upcoming July meeting, maintaining the 3.50-3.75% range. This outlook follows recent softer U.S. inflation data, which has reduced pressure for further monetary tightening. Improved risk sentiment in traditional markets is generally seen as supportive for cryptocurrency prices. However, some analysts caution that sustained demand for risk assets like crypto might be limited if inflation doesn't firmly hit the Fed's 2% target, potentially leading to a "higher-for-longer" rate scenario. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh recently emphasized supporting economic growth but also stated the Fed would not bail out crypto or stablecoins if they faced a crisis.
title: Fed Holds Rates Steady Amid Easing Inflation, Boosting Crypto Sentiment

details: July 18, 2026, marked the statutory deadline for six U.S. federal agencies to publish final stablecoin regulations as part of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act. This framework clarifies who can issue payment stablecoins in the U.S., detailing capital requirements, reserve composition, and licensing standards. While not resolving all questions, this represents a significant step towards regulatory clarity and is seen as crucial for the institutionalization of digital assets.
title: US Finalizes Stablecoin Regulations Under GENIUS Act

details: Spot Bitcoin ETFs have continued to experience net inflows, reversing earlier outflows, with Bitcoin funds attracting $132 million and Ethereum ETFs seeing $36.73 million in inflows on July 17. These institutional flows are increasingly driving the crypto market in 2026. Furthermore, Bitcoin whales have been actively accumulating BTC throughout the last two weeks, adding approximately 270,000 BTC, indicating strong buying interest from large investors.
title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs See Renewed Inflows, Whale Accumulation Continues

details: Field hearings for the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) were held on July 17 in New York, aimed at clarifying the jurisdictional boundaries between the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for "digital goods" and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for "investment contracts." While the bill's passage in 2026 remains uncertain with a decreased probability, the ongoing discussions are contributing to a sense of regulatory optimism that is helping to support the broader cryptocurrency market.
sourceName: Sergey Tereshkin (via a crypto news aggregator)
title: CLARITY Act Hearings Advance, Regulatory Optimism Builds
